documents.title: Syllabus Guidance for Generative AI
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance telling faculty to state their own generative AI expectations, suggesting three use levels and co-creating rules with students, and warning against blanket bans. It reproduces faculty sample statements from computing and other units, ranging from limited use with disclosure to required use.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule: it says approaches 'will vary by program, instructor, course, assessment' and offers 'three acceptable use levels', so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: The CTL says it 'strongly encourages the use of RIT-supported AI tools'. This recommends sanctioned tools to faculty, so P17 fits, with instructors as the actor.
units.anchor: strongly encourages the use of
units.fit_note: The encouragement is aimed at faculty, not a tool a course provides.

units.why: The CTL asks 'RIT faculty to clearly articulate their expectations for generative AI use'. This is about stating expectations, so P09 rather than P04.
units.anchor: RIT faculty to clearly articulate their expectations for generative AI use

units.why: 'it is important to clarify for yourself what the role of generative AI should be in your class' leaves the decision to each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: clarify for yourself what the role of generative AI should be in your class

units.why: The text advises to 'check with colleagues in your department' about their GenAI approach. No type covers departmental alignment; P63 (faculty learning about AI) is nearest.
units.anchor: check with colleagues in your department to see how they are addressing generative AI
units.fit_note: Peer consultation within the department, not workshops or training.

units.why: 'Approaches... will vary by program, instructor, course, assessment, and even by individual learning activities' says the rule is set per instructor and activity, so P04.
units.anchor: will vary by program, instructor, course, assessment, and even by individual learning activities

units.why: The guidance offers 'three acceptable use levels' (No AI use, Some AI use with restrictions, Open use of AI). These are named tiers, so P05.
units.anchor: outlining three acceptable use levels

units.why: It warns that 'a blanket statement prohibiting the use of generative AI can result in an adversarial situation'. This advises against a blanket ban; no type covers that, and P03 is about discouraging AI itself, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: a blanket statement prohibiting the use of generative AI can result in an adversarial situation
units.uncovered_note: Advises instructors against a blanket ban on generative AI because it creates an adversarial classroom.

units.why: 'faculty may wish to co-create expectations for the use of generative AI with students' is the co-creation type, P67.
units.anchor: co-create expectations for the use of generative AI with students

units.why: Faculty 'may also consider communicating their expectations... within individual assignment instructions, during course discussion, and within learning activities'. This extends communication beyond the syllabus; P66 fits better than P09, which is about the syllabus statement.
units.anchor: communicating their expectations for generative AI use within individual assignment instructions
units.fit_note: Concerns channels for communicating the rule, not explaining reasons.

units.why: 'Clearly communicating your expectations to students can reduce confusion... and promote academic integrity' gives the reason for stating expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: can reduce confusion on the role of generative AI in your classroom

units.why: The page says 'GenAI technology is incredibly dynamic and constantly evolving', acknowledging that rules must change; P54 is nearest.
units.anchor: incredibly dynamic and constantly evolving
units.fit_note: Notes the technology evolves and teaching needs agility; no commitment to review a policy.

units.why: The intro states the resource 'is intended to help faculty begin to address generative AI in RIT course policies and syllabi', a statement of purpose and scope, P56.
units.anchor: intended to help faculty begin to address generative AI in RIT course policies

units.why: Life Sciences sample: students 'are encouraged to explore the use of RIT-supported generative artificial intelligence tools such as Copilot or Gemini'. A default-encouraging course rule, P02.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to explore the use of RIT-supported generative artificial intelligence tools

units.why: 'any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' is a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited

units.why: The sample says acknowledgements go in 'in-text citations, quotations, or references in writing assignments, and comments in data analysis submissions'. This is where disclosure is placed; P27 is nearest.
units.anchor: in-text citations, quotations, or references in writing assignments, and comments in data analysis submissions
units.frag_start: Such acknowledgements can be done via
units.fit_note: Also allows in-text citation in prose, not only code comments.

units.why: 'Violations of this policy will be considered as academic misconduct' classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered as academic misconduct

units.why: 'It is your responsibility to assess the validity of any output generated by AI' tells students to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: responsibility to assess the validity of any output generated by AI

units.why: 'thorough modifications are highly recommended' because output 'rarely accomplishes the tasks to the level expected'. Students should heavily rework AI output; P32 is nearest.
units.anchor: thorough modifications are highly recommended when making use of these tools
units.fit_note: Recommends heavy editing of AI output as a starting point; not about the primary problem-solver role.

units.why: 'For the work that you submit, you bear the final responsibility' is student ownership, P29.
units.anchor: For the work that you submit, you bear the final responsibility

units.why: Lange CS sample: 'you are encouraged to work with generative AI tools in ways that let you practice good habits and that help you learn'. Default permission with conditions, P02.
units.anchor: you are encouraged to work with generative AI tools in ways that let you practice

units.why: 'we do not want generative AI tools to do your work' bars AI from producing submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: we do not want generative AI tools to do your work

units.why: 'Think about chat-based AI tools like a TA or classmate' treats AI as a human collaborator under existing rules, P45.
units.anchor: Think about chat-based AI tools like a TA or classmate

units.why: It lists 'Smart in-context code completion such as GitHub Copilot' as acceptable and encouraged if the student reads and confirms the generated body. This allows generated code under stated conditions, P16; P07 covers rules about built-in tools but not conditional acceptance.
units.anchor: Smart in-context code completion such as GitHub Copilot (free for students)
units.fit_note: Also covers editor-integrated completion and a duty to verify the generated code.

units.why: It permits 'a conversation with a chat-based LLM... about high-level concepts', tutor-like use, P12.
units.anchor: Having a conversation with a chat-based LLM (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) about high-level

units.why: It permits 'Asking it to explain a specific snippet of code (one or two functions, say)'. Explaining code to understand it fits P13 better than P12.
units.anchor: Asking it to explain a specific snippet of code (one or two functions, say)
units.fit_note: Explaining code snippets rather than error messages.

units.why: It permits 'Asking it to quiz you on course topics', self-testing, P14.
units.anchor: Asking it to quiz you on course topics

units.why: 'you take ultimate responsibility for the integrity of the code you submit' is student ownership, P29.
units.anchor: you take ultimate responsibility for the integrity of the code you submit

units.why: It disallows 'Sharing an account on a Chat model site with another student'. No type covers account sharing, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Sharing an account on a Chat model site with another
units.uncovered_note: Students may not share an account on a chat AI site with another student.

units.why: It disallows 'Uploading/pasting large sections of assignments with the intent of having the AI complete a portion'. The forbidden act is the upload, so P20 rather than P19.
units.anchor: Uploading/pasting large sections of assignments with the intent of having the AI complete
units.fit_note: The ban is limited to large sections pasted with intent to have AI complete work.

units.why: 'it is good practice to try out that code and try to understand how it works' asks students to understand generated code, P30.
units.anchor: good practice to try out that code and try to understand how it works

units.why: 'it is bad practice to "merely copy/paste" without understanding' discourages uncritical copying, P30.
units.anchor: But it is bad practice to

units.why: 'All assignments include a required “Collaboration and Generative AI disclosure” statement' is a disclosure with every submission, P24.
units.anchor: required “Collaboration and Generative AI disclosure” statement

units.why: Students who use a chat model 'are required to include a link to your chat history (if available) or paste in a transcript', P26.
units.anchor: include a link to your chat history (if available) or paste in a transcript of
units.frag_start: if you use a chat model,

units.why: Disallowed collaboration or AI misuse 'will result in a discussion with the instructor', a talk before escalation, P57.
units.anchor: will result in a discussion with the instructor

units.why: 'Repeat offenses may result in grade penalties' states a penalty escalated by offense, P37.
units.anchor: Repeat offenses may result in grade penalties

units.why: 'This policy is subject to change, but always as a result of discussion between instructor and students' commits to revising with students, P54.
units.anchor: subject to change, but always as a result of discussion between instructor and students

units.why: 'We will be using ChatGPT (or equivalent) to help develop course materials' discloses AI-made materials, P48.
units.anchor: We will be using ChatGPT (or equivalent) to help develop course materials

units.why: The instructor 'uses GitHub Copilot for his own daily coding, but he always carefully examines the outputs', disclosing his own AI use to students, P47.
units.anchor: uses GitHub Copilot for his own daily coding

units.why: 'learning to use new technologies effectively but also responsibly' gives a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: learning to use new technologies effectively but also responsibly

units.why: Liao CS sample defines generative AI and lists chatbots, OS assistants, code completion and art generators, setting the policy's scope. P61 chosen over P07 because it is a definition.
units.anchor: Generative AI refers to a type of artificial intelligence tools that accept user requests as
units.fit_note: The list includes OS-integrated assistants and IDE completion tools.

units.why: 'the rule of thumb is to treat it as if it were a human' sets AI under existing human-collaboration rules, P45.
units.anchor: the rule of thumb is to treat it as if it were a human
units.frag_start: the rule of thumb is to
units.frag_end: as if it were a human

units.why: 'you may use generative AI to do anything you are allowed to do with another person' is the same analogy as a permission, P45.
units.anchor: you may use generative AI to do anything you are allowed to do with another

units.why: Permitted: 'Asking generative AI about a concept in this course per se', P12.
units.anchor: Asking generative AI about a concept in this course per se

units.why: Prohibited: prompting AI 'to get solutions or reusable code for an assignment or an exam question', P19.
units.anchor: prompt generative AI to get solutions or reusable code for an assignment or an exam

units.why: Prohibited: 'adding any amount of assignment instructions and starter code to the prompt', P20.
units.anchor: adding any amount of assignment instructions and starter code to the prompt

units.why: Prohibited: 'Representing any amount of generative AI output as if it were your own work', P19.
units.anchor: Representing any amount of generative AI output as if it were your own work

units.why: Prohibited: 'Having generative AI check any work you submit for grading', P21.
units.anchor: Having generative AI check any work you submit for grading

units.why: Rationale: AI output 'is not your original work either, so you may not submit it for grading', tied to ownership, P29.
units.anchor: it is not your original work either, so you may not submit it for grading
units.fit_note: Explains why AI output does not count as the student's own work.

units.why: Rationale: pasting work into AI 'may be used to train an updated version', 'effectively equivalent to posting it online'. A data-protection reason, P50.
units.anchor: entering your work into generative AI could be effectively equivalent to posting it online
units.fit_note: Protects students' own work from training use, not personal data.

units.why: 'we reserve the right to require you to explain and/or recreate your work in an in-person, one-on-one meeting' checks understanding, P34.
units.anchor: require you to explain and/or recreate your work in an in-person, one-on-one meeting

units.why: 'it might output wrong information, so you should use caution and your own judgment', P31.
units.anchor: it might output wrong information, so you should use caution and your own judgment

units.why: It invites 'any questions, concerns, or suggestions regarding use of generative AI in this course'. Closest is P10 (ask), with a note.
units.anchor: any questions, concerns, or suggestions regarding use of generative AI
units.fit_note: Invites questions and suggestions generally, not asking before using AI.

units.why: School of Information sample: students 'are allowed and encouraged to utilize Generative AI tools as a resource for completing assignments', P02.
units.anchor: allowed and encouraged to utilize Generative AI tools as a resource for completing assignments

units.why: 'these resources are not a replacement for your learning and comprehension' keeps the student as primary learner, P32.
units.anchor: these resources are not a replacement for your learning and comprehension

units.why: 'all quizzes, exams, and the final practical... will be conducted without Internet access, meaning you cannot use Generative AI tools', P22.
units.anchor: all quizzes, exams, and the final practical for this course will be conducted without Internet

units.why: Reason given: 'Real-world situations often require quick thinking... without external aids'. Unassisted exams check foundations; P42 (fundamentals first) is nearest.
units.anchor: to accurately assess your understanding and readiness
units.fit_note: The reason is readiness for professional settings without aids.

units.why: The intent is 'ensuring that you are building a solid foundational understanding', fundamentals first, P42.
units.anchor: ensuring that you are building a solid foundational understanding of the course material

units.why: The goal 'to best prepare you for future professional scenarios' is a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: best prepare you for future professional scenarios
units.fit_note: Prepares students for settings without AI access.

units.why: 'it's expected that the work you submit will be your own, even when using AI tools to assist' is ownership, P29.
units.anchor: it's expected that the work you submit will be your own

units.why: It refers students to 'the department’s academic dishonesty policy' for external-resource use, P36.
units.anchor: refer to the department’s academic dishonesty policy
units.fit_note: Only points to the existing dishonesty policy.

units.why: Cybersecurity GenAI course: 'the expectation in this class is that you use Gen AI tools as much as possible', required use. P02 covers 'expects'.
units.anchor: the expectation in this class is that you use Gen AI tools as much as
units.fit_note: Use is required, beyond permitted or encouraged.

units.why: '“Cheating,” in this class, may constitute not using enough Gen AI' inverts misconduct; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: “Cheating,” in this class, may constitute not using enough Gen AI
units.uncovered_note: Not using enough generative AI counts as cheating in a course that requires AI use.

units.why: Students must 'include your own actual observations and reflections in your self-reflection submissions'. Reflections are P26, though these are not reflections on AI use.
units.anchor: include your own actual observations and reflections in your self-reflection submissions
units.fit_note: Requires the student's own reflections, not reflections on AI use.

units.why: The preface says the course will 'introduce cybersecurity students to real-world uses of GenAI in the field', teaching AI as a professional skill, P44.
units.anchor: introduce cybersecurity students to real-world uses of GenAI in the field

units.why: MECE 200: AI 'may be inaccurate or used in a way that hampers effective concept learning', a warning about accuracy, P31.
units.anchor: provides information that may be inaccurate or used in a way that hampers effective concept

units.why: 'The most restrictive is their forbidden use during exams and quizzes', P22.
units.anchor: forbidden use during exams and quizzes

units.why: 'The least restrictive is their use in concept review, studying, and support (excluding content)' on homework, P14.
units.anchor: use in concept review, studying, and support (excluding content) in the completion of homework

units.why: 'students are allowed to use AI in limited ways as described further below' is a default permission that is narrow and listed. P02 is nearest but the stance is restrict.
units.anchor: students are allowed to use AI in limited ways
units.frag_start: The General Policy about AI use
units.fit_note: Permission is narrow and listed, closer to restrict.

units.why: 'AI tools are limited to Google Gemini and Microsoft 365 Copilot. No other AI chatbots are permitted', limits AI to sanctioned tools, P17.
units.anchor: No other AI chatbots are permitted for use with this course
units.fit_note: Limits use to two named RIT-supported tools.

units.why: 'Only to formulate alternative meaning to specific engineering topics with the intention of developing deeper understanding' allows concept explanation only, P12.
units.anchor: Only to formulate alternative meaning to specific engineering topics

units.why: 'Only with proper citations and acknowledgement' is a disclosure condition, P24.
units.anchor: Only with proper citations and acknowledgement

units.why: 'AI will not be used to generate content for graded assignments' bars AI-produced submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: AI will not be used to generate content for graded assignments

units.why: Students are 'responsible for identifying and addressing any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or problematic AI-generated content', P31.
units.anchor: responsible for identifying and addressing any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or problematic AI-generated content

units.why: 'Students must disclose the use of AI... citing the source and the prompt used' requires tool, prompt and way of use, P25.
units.anchor: citing the source and the prompt used to solicit the information

units.why: 'Students must cite AI outputs following IEEE standards and guidelines' fixes a citation style, P25.
units.anchor: Students must cite AI outputs following

units.why: 'AI must not be used as an alternative to developing and acquiring sufficient conceptual understanding' limits AI because practice builds skill, P41.
units.anchor: AI must not be used as an alternative to developing and acquiring sufficient conceptual understanding

units.why: 'Students may create free accounts for RIT ITS supported tools' provides free access, P51.
units.anchor: Students may create free accounts for

documents.title: D08.0 Student Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: The university integrity policy mentions AI in two lines only. Unapproved AI methods and AI content without authorization or citation count as cheating and plagiarism.
documents.stance_why: It lists 'unapproved artificial intelligence (AI) methods' as cheating, so AI is banned unless approved, which is restrict.

units.why: The integrity policy lists as cheating 'Using unauthorized materials, sources, or tools, including unapproved artificial intelligence (AI) methods'. That classifies unauthorized AI as cheating, P36.
units.anchor: including unapproved artificial intelligence (AI) methods for assignments, exams, or assessments
units.frag_start: Using unauthorized materials, sources, or tools,

units.why: Under plagiarism it lists 'Using AI-generated content without authorization or citation'. Missing authorization or citation is plagiarism, P36; the disclosure aspect is secondary.
units.anchor: Using AI-generated content without authorization or citation
units.fit_note: Also implies AI content needs authorization or citation.

notes: Syllabus page is university-layer CTL guidance but most units come from faculty sample statements (Lange and Liao CS; Arcoraci iSchool; Cybersecurity; MECE; Life Sciences). Topic codes are my own slugs because AGENT_BRIEF.md was not present.
